title: Optimization Suggestions (Console) — Beta Kickoff Notes
content:
Doc: Optimization Suggestions (Console) — Beta kickoff notes
Last updated: 2026-02-24

Meeting 1 (kickoff): 2026-01-21, 10:00–11:00 PT
Meeting 2 (follow-up): 2026-02-04, 10:30–11:00 PT

Attendees (core):
- Marissa Cole (PM, Console)
- Aditya Rao (PM, Optimize)
- Dylan Brooks (Eng lead, Console)
- Chloe Martin (Eng lead, Console backend)
- Tessa Morgan (Design)
- Logan Wright (Telemetry)
- Dr. Maya Srinivasan (Applied ML sponsor)
- Miguel Santos (CS, beta program)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE rollout)

Agenda
1) Beta scope alignment (what ships vs what does not)
2) End-to-end experience: Suggestions view -> details -> apply path
3) Data + estimator needs and confidence/risk labeling
4) API contract + stable IDs + pagination
5) Rollout plan: feature flag gating + target accounts + support readiness
6) Open questions + owners


High-level goal (why we’re doing this)
- Make cost optimization actionable in the Console by surfacing top batching/caching opportunities by route/model with clear estimated savings, estimated performance impact (p50/p95 deltas), and a conservative risk label (Low/Medium/High) with guardrails.
- Build trust: show assumptions + where data comes from; no implied guarantees.
- Close the loop: instrument impressions → expand → dismiss → apply.


Scope (Beta = batching/caching only)
In scope (beta):
- Console: Suggestions list/table view + details drawer
  - Filters: org/project, environment, route, model, region (subject to data availability)
  - Sorting: by estimated $ saved/day, % saved, risk, confidence
  - Empty/error states + onboarding CTAs
  - Deep links to relevant config pages (batching/caching settings)
- Backend: /optimize/suggestions endpoint
  - Pagination + stable IDs
  - RBAC: read scope + audit logging
- Estimation pipeline: v0 savings estimator + risk scoring v0
  - Conservative defaults, confidence band, “stale as of”
- Observability: API health + compute lag + funnel dashboard
- Beta program: feature flag per org; limited accounts; feedback intake workflow

Explicitly NOT in scope (beta):
- Quantization recommendations UI (can be referenced as “coming next” but no launch)
- Auto-apply suggestions (no background changes; user-driven only)
- Contractual savings guarantees

Decision note:
- We will call this “Optimization Suggestions (Beta)” and keep copy tight on “estimated” + “based on last N days of traffic.”


User + persona assumptions
Primary persona (beta):
- Platform/infra engineer or ML engineer responsible for serving configuration + cost/perf.
Secondary persona:
- Engineering manager reviewing “why did our costs spike?” and looking for quick levers.

User problems we’re targeting:
- “I know I’m overspending but I don’t know which route/model is the worst offender.”
- “I’m afraid batching/caching will violate latency SLOs.”
- “I don’t trust opaque ‘savings’ claims.”


Early UX direction (notes from Design)
List/table:
- Rows represent a suggestion for (project, route, model, region) tuple. (Final exact grouping TBD; see Open Qs.)
- Columns (proposed):
  - Suggestion (title)
  - Estimated savings (e.g., $/day + %)
  - Performance impact (p50/p95 delta)
  - Risk (badge)
  - Confidence (simple label + tooltip)
  - Last updated / stale as of
- Clicking a row opens a right-side details drawer.

Details drawer (must-have sections):
- “Why we recommend this” (top 2–3 driver signals)
- “Estimated impact” (savings + latency deltas + confidence band)
- “Risk and guardrails” (risk label + what could go wrong + how to roll out safely)
- “How to apply” (deep link to batching/caching config, plus suggested values)
- “Data used” (lookback window + traffic thresholds + last computed)

Copy/education:
- Risk should be framed as performance/reliability risk (NOT security risk).
- Use consistent language: “Estimated” “Expected range” “Based on observed traffic.”

Mock links (early / WIP):
- Figma (WIP): figma://redwood/console/optimize-suggestions/beta-table-v1
- Drawer copy draft (WIP): gdoc://product/console-and-rollouts/suggestions-drawer-copy-v0
(These are placeholders in this working doc; final links should live in the Confluence design spec.)


API + data notes (kickoff discussion)
Proposed API responsibilities:
- List endpoint returns N suggestions with stable IDs + enough preview fields for table.
- Details endpoint (or list item expanded fields) returns full explanation, assumptions, and recommended config values.
- Include “stale_as_of” and “inputs_coverage” (e.g., % of traffic covered by telemetry) so UI can show data quality.

Telemetry signals called out as “must-have” (v0):
- Request rate (QPS / req/day) by route/model/region
- Token counts / sequence length distribution (prompt+gen)
- Latency distributions (p50/p95) baseline
- Current batching config and observed batch sizes (where available)
- Cache hit rates (prefix/KV) and cache-eligible fraction
- Error rates/timeouts (baseline) to avoid recommending on already unstable routes

Pipeline cadence:
- Prefer batch job (hourly or daily) to avoid heavy per-request compute.
- Need to communicate in UI: “updated X hours ago” and/or “computed daily.”


Risk labels (working alignment)
Risk label goal:
- One simple badge for “how likely this is to cause performance/reliability regressions if applied as recommended.”

Risk is NOT:
- Not a security/privacy risk.
- Not a “business risk” score.

Initial mapping (subject to ADR finalization):
- Low: Suggestion is within conservative guardrails; predicted p95 impact minimal; enough traffic to be confident.
- Medium: Some uncertainty in latency impact; or route has tighter latency SLO/low headroom.
- High: Suggestion may increase p95 meaningfully, or data is sparse/variable; requires careful staged rollout.

UI behavior idea:
- High risk suggestions should always show “recommended rollout steps” and a warning callout.


Rollout & beta program notes
Feature flag:
- Org-level flag for “optimize_suggestions_beta” (exact name TBD).
- Keep server-side checks aligned with RBAC and org/project scoping.

Beta selection criteria (Miguel/CS + PM):
- Telemetry maturity: must have required signals + stable traffic
- Cost sensitivity: meaningful spend to see impact
- Operational maturity: has someone to apply changes + observe impact

Support readiness:
- Prepare canned responses for:
  1) “estimate doesn’t match billing”
  2) “no suggestions but we have traffic”
  3) “risk label is confusing / escalations from stakeholders”
- Ensure docs explain that savings are estimates; not a guarantee.

Success metrics (beta):
- Funnel: impression → expand → apply-click rate
- Dismissal reasons (structured)
- Post-apply monitoring (qualitative in beta): did latency / error rates regress? did cost change?
- API health: p95 latency + error rate for suggestions endpoint


Open questions (with owners)
1) What is the exact grouping key for a “suggestion” row?
   - Option A: route+model+region
   - Option B: route+model (region folded)
   - Option C: route only (model variants folded)
   Owner: Marissa + Chloe + Logan
   Notes: We need a grouping that aligns with config knobs (often per route) but still actionable when multiple models behind a route.

2) Lookback window for estimates (7d vs 14d vs 30d) and how to handle seasonality?
   Owner: Maya + Jonas + Nadia
   Notes: Risk/confidence should degrade gracefully for shorter windows. UI must display “based on last X days.”

3) Confidence representation: numeric (0–1), label (High/Med/Low), or “data quality” indicator?
   Owner: Tessa + George + Sana
   Notes: We should test comprehension; avoid false precision.

4) Latency delta reporting: show absolute ms vs percent vs both?
   Owner: Tessa + Dylan
   Notes: Some users prefer ms; others rely on % for comparisons. Might show “+12ms (p95), +4%” in drawer.

5) Guardrails: when do we refuse to generate a suggestion (hard constraints)?
   Owner: Aditya + Hassan + Sean
   Notes: e.g., do not recommend batching above X for routes with p95 < 300ms target; do not recommend caching if cache hit uplift uncertain.

6) “Apply” definition in funnel tracking.
   - Is apply = user clicks deep link? or apply = config saved? or apply = rollout completed?
   Owner: Logan + Dylan + Marissa
   Notes: For beta, at minimum track deep link click + config save event if available.

7) RBAC: which roles can view suggestions vs apply changes?
   Owner: Kaitlyn + Marcus + Chloe
   Notes: Expect at least read-only roles to view. Applying is controlled by existing config permission. Ensure audit logs for access.

8) Empty states taxonomy:
   - No data yet vs insufficient telemetry vs feature not enabled vs no opportunities found
   Owner: Kenji + Nora + George

9) Staleness behavior:
   - When data pipeline lags, do we hide suggestions, show last computed with banner, or degrade confidence?
   Owner: Mei + Yara + Sean


Action items (from kickoff)
- Marissa: finalize PRD draft + align with Aditya on explicit non-goals (quantization UI, auto-apply). Due: 2026-01-28
- Chloe: propose API shape (list + details) and stable ID strategy; circulate for review. Due: 2026-01-29
- Dylan: draft front-end implementation plan (table, filters, drawer, error states) with perf considerations. Due: 2026-02-03
- Tessa/Kenji: produce updated wireframes for table + drawer + empty states. Due: 2026-02-05
- Logan/Nadia: confirm telemetry availability + gaps; propose event taxonomy for funnel. Due: 2026-02-06
- Maya/Jonas/Sana: share v0 estimator assumptions + risk threshold proposal + how we’ll validate. Due: 2026-02-10
- Miguel: draft beta target account criteria + initial candidate list (top ~10). Due: 2026-02-12
- Sean: draft rollout/rollback criteria and basic oncall readiness plan for beta. Due: 2026-02-14


Risks / watch-outs (captured verbatim)
- “If we show a big $/day number and it’s wrong, we lose trust immediately.” (Aditya)
- “Risk badge can’t be interpreted as security risk—needs explicit tooltip language.” (Tessa)
- “API p95 must be tight; this page will be used during incident triage and can’t be sluggish.” (Dylan)
- “We need a clear explanation for ‘insufficient telemetry’ or it’ll generate support volume.” (Miguel)

Mitigation ideas (beta):
- Conservative savings defaults; show ranges; show underlying assumptions; avoid overly precise decimals.
- Add “stale_as_of” and pipeline health to empty states.
- Keep per-request runtime overhead near zero by relying on aggregates.


Notes / parking lot
- Quantization: Align messaging: “coming soon” but do not show disabled UI that looks broken.
- Consider A/B test between two confidence label schemes (if low lift).
- Consider ‘dismiss reason’ dropdown to improve learning loop (e.g., “not relevant,” “don’t trust estimate,” “can’t change config,” “latency too risky”).

Next check-ins
- Weekly product/eng sync: Tuesdays 9:30–10:00 PT (temporary for beta build)
- Design critique for updated wireframes: 2026-02-06
- Beta readiness review (go/no-go for first cohort): target week of 2026-03-02

Changelog
- 2026-02-04: Added risk/confidence open questions; added apply definition discussion.
- 2026-02-24: Updated action items + beta program notes; added staleness/empty state taxonomy item.
